# OSBB

One shared bulletin board: named people talk with each other and one agent on a
single replayable session.

OSBB exists to make Agentyk's multi-actor contract visible. Each person's input
is a `Message` carrying an `ExternalActor`; the event log keeps the original
text and identity, while the model sees speaker labels such as `[Ada]` and
`[Grace]`.

<img src="docs/demo.gif" width="880" alt="Ada and Grace taking turns in one OSBB session while Archivist tracks each named speaker and helps them reach a decision.">

<sup>Recorded on `openai/gpt-5.6-terra`. Displayed at half its pixel width for a
crisp terminal capture.</sup>

## Run it

```sh
export OPENAI_API_KEY=...
cargo run --release -p osbb
```

Defaults are intentionally ready for the demo:

```text
One shared bulletin board for named people and an agent.

Usage: osbb [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --people <PEOPLE>                    Comma-separated display names [default: Ada,Grace]
      --actor <ACTOR>
      --agent-name <AGENT_NAME>            Display name of the agent [default: Archivist]
      --model <MODEL>                      OpenAI model id [default: gpt-5.6-terra]
      --base-url <BASE_URL>
      --reasoning-effort <REASONING_EFFORT> [default: none]
      --log <LOG>
  -h, --help
  -V, --version
```

Inside the room:

```text
/as NAME  speak as another person
/who      show everyone on the board
/help     show help
/quit     leave the board
```

Plain text belongs to the currently selected person. OSBB rejects unknown
names instead of silently creating participants.

## What it proves

- Ada and Grace append to one `Session`, so each turn sees the full shared
  history.
- `ExternalActor { source, actor_id, actor_name }` survives event-log replay.
- Provider-facing context labels each user without rewriting the durable
  message.
- The UI has no participant database. Membership, roles, and authorization
  remain responsibilities of an embedding host such as Everruns.

The offline test runs two named people through the real executor with
`SimDriver` and inspects both raw history and recorded model requests:

```sh
cargo test -p osbb
```

## Re-recording the demo

The GIF is a real `gpt-5.6-terra` run recorded with
[VHS](https://github.com/charmbracelet/vhs) and compressed with
[gifsicle](https://www.lcdf.org/gifsicle/):

```sh
cargo build --release -p osbb
PATH="$PWD/target/release:$PATH" OPENAI_API_KEY=... vhs examples/osbb/demo.tape
gifsicle -O3 --lossy=60 --colors 64 -b examples/osbb/docs/demo.gif
```

[`demo.tape`](demo.tape) records at 2× density and this README displays the
result at half width, matching Codenko's sharp HiDPI demo convention.
